brief: A support inbox gets bug reports, feature requests and angry complaints. Sort each one and send the right reply.

buildPhases.coach: Let's build. First — what should start this flow?
buildPhases.label: Set your trigger

buildPhases.coach: Trigger's set. Now let's make it read and understand each email.
buildPhases.label: Give it a brain

buildPhases.coach: It can read emails now. Last part — route by category and send the right reply.
buildPhases.label: Route & reply

coverImage.alt: A retro computer streaming an email up into three sorting bins
coverImage.prompt: A single retro pixel-art computer on the left, and three simple cube trays on the right, with one envelope travelling between them on a short stream of binary. Wide, sparse, left to right.

difficultyNote: One router, three branches, and every node needs configuring.

dissection.explanation: A New Email trigger fires the moment a support email lands — exactly the signal this workflow needs to react to.
dissection.prompt: Let’s start at the very top. Which app should kick this workflow off?
dissection.wrongHint: Think about what has to be watching the inbox in real time. Does this one actually do that?

dissection.explanation: Classify with AI reads the message the way a person would and labels it — resilient to however the email is phrased. It’ll need a language model plugged in, which you’ll wire up later.
dissection.prompt: A raw email just came in. What should read it and work out what kind of email it is?
dissection.wrongHint: The email is messy, free-form text. Would fixed rules or code reliably tell a bug apart from a complaint?

dissection.explanation: Parse Result turns the AI’s text into clean fields — category and urgency — so every node after it can read them reliably.
dissection.prompt: The AI hands its answer back as one blob of text. What comes next, before you can branch on it?
dissection.wrongHint: Right now it’s just a string of text. Can the next node reliably branch on that as-is?

dissection.explanation: Switch routes a single input to as many labelled outputs as you define — one each for Bug Report, Feature Request and Urgent Complaint.
dissection.prompt: Three categories, three different replies. Which node sends one input down several paths by rule?
dissection.wrongHint: You need one item to go down three separate paths by rule. Does this node give you that many outputs?

dissection.explanation: Send Reply emails the customer back with a message tailored to their category — the whole point of the triage.
dissection.prompt: Last decision. At the end of each branch, what actually responds to the customer?
dissection.wrongHint: The customer reached out over email. Would this option actually get a response back to them?

evalQuestions.explanation: Your Switch only has 3 branches — Bug Report, Feature Request, Urgent Complaint. A plain question matches none of them, so it silently falls through and no reply is ever sent. Real automations need a default/catch-all branch for exactly this.
options: It gets logged as a Feature Request by default
It doesn't match any of the 3 defined paths, so nothing sends
The flow throws an error and stops
It is automatically escalated as Urgent Complaint
evalQuestions.prompt: A customer email arrives that's just a general question, with no bug/feature/complaint keywords. What happens in this flow?

evalQuestions.explanation: The workflow is deterministic: the AI does exactly one job — classify — and everything else (parse, route, reply) is fixed wiring you designed. A full agent would decide its own steps and tools at runtime, which is powerful but unpredictable. For reliable, repeatable triage, a fixed path is the right call.
options: Because Gemini cannot be used in an autonomous agent
Because n8n does not support branching logic
Because the structure is fixed and predictable — the AI only does one classification step, it doesn't choose which tools to call
Because fixed-path classifiers are always more accurate than agents
evalQuestions.prompt: Why is this modeled as a fixed-path classifier rather than a full autonomous agent choosing tools?

flowSummary.caption: Three categories, three replies. One AI step decides which, and the split sends each down its own path.

fields.label: Temperature
fields.subtitle: How much the model is allowed to vary its answer between runs.
fields.whyCorrect: Right. At 0 the model gives the same answer for the same email every time. Triage has to be repeatable — the same complaint should never be a Bug Report on Monday and a Complaint on Tuesday.
fields.whyWrong: Anything above 0 lets the model pick differently on identical input. That is useful when you want variety in writing, and the opposite of what you want when the answer decides which branch an email takes. What value makes it deterministic?

fields.label: Text to classify
fields.subtitle: Drag the field from Input, or type the expression yourself.
fields.whyCorrect: Right — the message body is the content being judged, and referencing it as an expression means every email gets read, not just this one.
fields.whyWrong: Look at what the Input pane is offering. One of those fields holds the customer’s actual complaint; the others hold who sent it and what they titled it. And if you typed the text in directly, ask yourself what happens on the next email.

fields.label: How should it return the answer?

options.label: JSON — { category, urgency }
options.why: Structured fields the Parse and Switch steps can read reliably.

options.label: A written paragraph
options.why: Free text is hard to branch on — you’d be back to square one.

options.label: A single word
options.why: You’d lose the urgency, and one loose word is brittle to parse.

fields.subtitle: The shape the next nodes can rely on.

locked.label: System prompt
locked.value: Classify this email as Bug Report, Feature Request or Complaint, with an urgency.

why.continueErrorOutput: Right. If classification fails, the email is routed somewhere you can see, instead of vanishing or taking the whole inbox down with it.
why.continueRegularOutput: This carries on with nothing to work from, so the email reaches the Switch with no category, matches no branch, and quietly disappears. Try it — pull the Chat Model out and run the flow.
why.stopWorkflow: One failure now halts everything behind it, and every email still queued goes unanswered until somebody notices. Is one bad classification worth stopping the inbox?

fields.subtitle: One rule per branch. Each rule names an output and says which emails go down it.

categories.correct: These are exactly the labels the AI assigns, so each branch can actually match something.
categories.wrong: A branch can only fire if something upstream produces its label. Look at what the Classify step actually outputs, and name the branches after those.

conditions.correct: Each branch tests the category the AI assigned, matched exactly. That is what makes the routing predictable.
conditions.wrong: Check what each branch is testing. The value to route on is the label the AI assigned — not how urgent it is, and not the raw text — and it should match exactly.

count.correct: Three branches for the three categories the AI can produce. Every category has somewhere to go.
count.wrong: Count what the classifier can output — three categories — and give each one its own branch. Too few and some emails have nowhere to go; too many and a branch can never fire.

fields.label: Emails matching no rule

options.label: Fall through — no reply sent
options.why: With only three branches, anything else silently falls through — that’s the gap the stress test asks about.

options.label: Send it down the first branch
options.why: That would mislabel unrelated mail as a bug report.

options.label: Throw an error
options.why: A non-match isn’t an error — the Switch simply has no matching output.

fields.subtitle: What happens to an email that matches none of your rules.

why.false: Correct — leave it off. When an email matches no branch, the Switch should produce nothing. That email going unanswered is a real gap you can see and fix; it is not something to paper over.
why.true: Turn this on and an email that matched nothing is still pushed down the first branch as an empty item — so a blank reply goes out to a real customer. Silently wrong is worse than visibly missing. Run it and watch the general question.

options.label: Spam

sampleCases.subject: App crashes every time I log in
Could you add a dark mode?

statement: Your inbox is full of mixed feedback. Build a flow that watches for new emails, uses AI to classify each one (Bug Report / Feature Request / Complaint), and routes urgent complaints differently from everything else — each path sends the right reply.
tagline: Classify incoming support emails with AI and route each to the right reply.

testCases.description: A New Email trigger starts the flow.
A Chat Model is plugged into the Classify with AI node.
The email is classified with AI, then the result is parsed.
A Switch node routes the parsed result by category.
Each branch reaches its own Send Reply node (Bug Report, Feature Request, Urgent Complaint).

title: Email Triage Automation
